title: PRD: multi-cohort sentinel ladder and adaptive cooldowns for Optimize evals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This PRD defines a new multi-cohort evaluation contract and automated rollback choreography for Redwood Optimize. The goal is to detect and act on regressions with high signal-to-noise across product cohorts while minimizing unnecessary rollbacks. The system blends stratified prompt cohorts, ensemble signals (quality, safety, latency, cost), and a staged ladder of sentinels + adaptive cooldowns for canaries and ramped rollouts.
background: Optimize currently uses single-threshold alerts and coarse-grained canaries for model rollouts. With growing variety of customer cohorts and production traffic shapes, we observe false positive rollbacks and delayed detection for cohort-specific regressions. This work standardizes acceptance criteria, introduces cohort-level sentinels, and adds cooldown/acceptance windows to reduce flapping.
goals: Define stratified prompt cohorts and sampling rules so evals represent production distribution
Specify composite regression thresholds and weightings across quality, safety, latency, and token cost
Create a sentinel ladder: private canary -> percent ramp -> global canary with clear stop rules
Introduce adaptive cooldowns to prevent immediate rollback flips after transient signals
Produce clear acceptance criteria and test harness for QA and platform owners
out_of_scope: Deep changes to runtime kernel selection
success_metrics: Reduction in false-positive rollbacks by >= 50% within 8 weeks of rollout
Median time-to-detect cohort regressions reduced to <= 30 minutes for high-impact cohorts
No more than 1 unintended global rollback per quarter after stabilization
signal_definitions: Quality: task-specific accuracy / pass-rate measured on labeled prompt cohorts
Safety: rate of flagged outputs per 1k responses on adversarial safety probes
Cost: median token-unit cost change relative to baseline model variant
Latency: p95 end-to-end inference latency for the cohort's typical sequence length
composite_thresholds: Minor degradation: any single signal crosses 1.5x baseline and composite score >= 0.3
Major degradation: any single signal crosses 2.0x baseline or composite score >= 0.6
Composite score computed as weighted sum: quality(0.45), safety(0.35), latency(0.15), cost(0.05)
cohorting_strategy: Define cohorts by product surface + token length bin + geographic region
Maintain a stable set of 12 sentinel cohorts initially (product teams to nominate representative flows)
Sampling: stratified reservoir sampling with minimum N=500 samples per cohort per evaluation window
sentinel_ladder: Stage 0: Private canary (internal traffic) for smoke checks
Stage 1: 0.5% traffic canary for target cohort(s) with 60-minute observation window
Stage 2: 5% ramp to cohort(s) for 6 hours with rolling analysis every 15 minutes
Stage 3: 25% cross-cohort ramp with 24-hour acceptance window and final global promotion
cooldown_policy: After a rollback action, enforce a cooldown period of 4 hours before reattempting same model variant
Cooldown extends by factor 2 if repeated rollbacks occur within a 30-day window
Temporary suspensions: if major degradation is detected, pause further rollouts until a mitigation PRD is approved
acceptance_criteria: Automated eval pipeline computes cohort metrics and composite score for every candidate model build
Canary passes Stage 1 with composite < 0.3 and no single-signal major degradation for 60-minute window
Stage 2 and 3 ramps must maintain composite < 0.4 averaged over the observation windows
If safety signal crosses major threshold at any stage, immediate rollback and incident page escalation
All rollbacks must include a minimal postmortem and a regression ticket within 2 business days
ab_criteria: A/B tests for feature change or model variant require minimum sample sizes: 10k impressions per variant or 3 days, whichever is later
Statistical test: two-sided proportion z-test for pass-rates with alpha=0.01 for quality metrics
Decision rules: prefer conservative thresholds for safety signals; require both statistical significance and practical delta (>=2% absolute) before promoting
playbook_actions: Automated rollback triggers on major degradation; page on-call SRE and PM
Soft-fail: if minor degradation occurs, trigger canary hold and notify owning PM/engineer with suggested mitigations
Escalation ladder: SRE -> Runtime eng -> Model owner -> VP product for unresolved major regressions
testing_plan: Unit tests for composite-scoring code path and simulated signal inputs
Synthetic regression injections across cohorts to validate sensitivity and false positive rate
Staging runbook: deploy changes to staging cluster and run A/B harness across sentinel cohorts for 48 hours
Chaos tests: simulate traffic surges and delayed metrics to validate cooldown behavior
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards for per-cohort signal trends and composite score heatmap
Alert thresholds mapped to PagerDuty severity levels and runbook links
Audit log of rollout decisions, timestamps, and responsible owners stored for 180 days
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal dogfooding on private canary for 2 weeks
Phase B: pilot with 3 production cohorts and telemetry validation for 3 weeks
Phase C: full platform default for new Optimize rollouts after 6 weeks and required training materials published
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: overfitting thresholds to historical noise -> Mitigation: periodic re-calibration using sliding window baseline
Risk: increased evaluation cost -> Mitigation: adaptive sampling and prioritizing cohorts by customer revenue impact
Risk: delayed detection for low-volume cohorts -> Mitigation: synthetic amplification and aggregate signals across similar cohorts
stakeholders: Engineering leads: Marcus Rivera (Optimize), Priya Singh (Runtime)
tasks: Define cohort list and nominate product owners
Implement composite scoring service and unit tests
Add dashboards and alert rules in monitoring stack
Create training docs and runbook for PMs and SREs
Pilot rollout with 3 cohorts and capture post-pilot learnings
notes: This PRD intentionally biases toward conservative promotion rules for safety. We will iterate weighting after pilot based on calibrated false-positive / false-negative tradeoffs.
decision_log: 3/10/2026 - PM+Eng agreed on composite weighting and 12 sentinel cohorts; 3/11/2026 - SRE proposed 4-hour cooldown baseline; 3/12/2026 - Security confirmed no sensitive-data telemetry required for sentinels
follow_up: Schedule calibration workshop with data scientists (by 2026-03-18)
Create pilot success dashboard and acceptance signoff form
